sentences.text: Petitioners

being accused Nos.1 to 5 in C.C.No.637/
2024 on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Shorapur [for short, 'the Trial Court']
(in Crime No.6/2024 of Kembhavi Police Station), are seeking to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against them for the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 323, 354, 498A, 504, 506 read with Section 149 of IPC.

2. Heard Sri Arunkumar Amargundappa, learned counsel for the petitioners and Smt. Arati Patil,
learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 - State.
Respondent No.2 though served, has remained un- represented.

3. In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4443 HC-KAR Whether the criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioners is liable to be quashed invoking inherent power under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023?

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4. Respondent No.2 has filed first information with Kembhavi Police Station against accused Nos.1 to 5 alleging commission of the offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 323, 354, 498A, 504,
506 read with Section 149 of IPC, and the FIR came to be registered in Crime No.6/2024 of Kembhavi Police Station on 11.01.2024.

As per the allegations made in the first information, the incident had occurred on 25.12.2023 and the reason for the delay in filing the first information is that she discussed with her relatives and filed the first information belatedly.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4443 HC-KAR 5.
The materials on record disclose that, respondent No.2 had married accused No.1 on 15.04.2022.
Only for some period she resided in the matrimonial house and thereafter she returned to her parental house.

The petitioners have produced copy of the agreement styled as "Vivaha Vichedana Oppanda Patra"
dated 06.06.2023.

As per this agreement entered into between accused No.1 and respondent No.2 in the presence of other witnesses referred to therein, respondent No.2 has accepted a sum of Rs.11,00,000/- to give consent for dissolution of marriage.
The document also refers to payment of Rs.11,00,000/- to respondent No.2 by accused No.1 in the presence of witnesses.

sentences.text: It is stated that, respondent No.2 has filed Crl.Misc.No.231/2023 before the learned Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Shorapur during October, 2023 claiming maintenance against accused No.1 under Section 125 Cr.P.C.
The same is pending consideration and in the meantime the present complaint came to be filed.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4443 HC-KAR 7.

On perusal of the first information lodged by respondent No.2, for commission of the offence punishable under Section 498A, it is to be noticed that bald and general allegations without any specific details are made.

However, it is stated that on 25.12.2023 at 6.00 a.m. accused Nos.1 to 5 came to her parents' house, abused respondent No.2 in filthy language, accused No.1 pulled her hair, assaulted and kicked her, accused Nos.2 and 5 assaulted her with hands, accused No.4 tried to outrage her modesty and all the accused have criminally intimidated her.
8.

After taking into consideration the fact that the petitioner has produced copy of the document styled as "Vivaha Vichedana Oppanda Patra" dated 06.06.2023 to contend that during June, 2023 respondent No.2 has accepted a sum of Rs.11,00,000/- and the marriage was dissolved in the presence of panchas, and later filed the first information belatedly assumes importance.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4443 HC-KAR Repeatedly notices were issued to respondent No.2 through Court/police and also by serving the counsel representing respondent No.2 in Crl.Misc.No.231/2023.
Inspite of that she remained absent and has not chosen to appear before the Court.
All these facts and circumstances give rise to a reasonable doubt about the contention taken by respondent No.2 regarding commission of the offence.

Even though the agreement styled as "Vivaha Vichedana Oppanda Patra"
relied by the petitioners will not have any legal sanctity to contend that there was dissolution of marriage, the fact remains that, as per this document, a hefty sum of Rs.11,00,000/- was paid by accused No.1 to respondent No.2 for dissolution of marriage.

If this fact is to be admitted, the contention of respondent No.2 that, on 25.12.2023 all the accused came and committed the offence in her parental house is hard to believe, that too when Crl.Misc.No.231/2023 was filed during October,2023 seeking maintenance from accused No.1.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4443 HC-KAR 9.
The Investigating Officer has investigated into the matter and filed the charge sheet.
No wound certificate is produced along with the final report.

If the allegations made by respondent No.2 is to be taken into consideration, she must have sustained injuries when accused Nos.1 to 5 have brutally assaulted her, kicked her and tried to outrage her modesty.

In the absence of any such prima facie materials, I am of the opinion that continuation of criminal proceedings against the petitioners is in abuse of process of law, and the same is liable to be quashed.

Accordingly, I answer the Yallappa And Ors vs The State Of Karnataka And Anr on 5 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/198232030/
4 above point in the 'affirmative' and proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The petition is allowed.
